brief: A tool caddy with a carry handle and divided bins for screws and bits.

requirements.evidence: Three full cells in a row (piece -1,0,0 / 0,0,0 / 1,0,0), joined with joint bolts (lockJoints) and with every open face capped (capOpenFaces). check_build found no issues and the mesh check is clear.
handle:0,0,0;top sits on the centre cover (cover:0,0,0;full;top), held by three inserts. The configurator checks fit only, not whether it is strong enough to lift a loaded caddy.
bin:1,0,0~hex-bin-half-div3 is a half-depth bin with 3 compartments, shown with piles of screws, nuts and standoffs.

bin:-1,0,0~hex-bin-full-div3 is a full-depth bin with 3 compartments for bits and drivers. The catalog has no bit prop, so a pen and a marker stand in it for show. Longer drivers and files tipped over when stood in it.

finish.summary: I built a 3-cell tool caddy in a straight row. The middle cell has a top cover with a carry handle on it. The two outer cells hold divided bins: a half-depth 3-compartment bin for screws and a full-depth 3-compartment bin for bits and drivers. Every open face has an end cap, and the joints between cells are bolted together. check_build found no issues and the mesh-collision check reads clear. The props are just for show: M3 screws, nuts and standoffs in the screw bin, and a pen and a marker standing in the deeper bin. The catalog has no driver-bit prop, so that bin shows those instead. All props show from above, but from the side the low screw piles sit below the bin rims. The parts weigh about 1586 g (30 parts).

lines.label: M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
